Action Plan:
1. Acute unilateral headache with migraine features  
   • Begin ibuprofen (dose/route/frequency not documented) plus over-the-counter anti-sickness medication (dose/route/frequency not documented) and drink a sugary carbonated beverage (e.g., Coca-Cola) immediately.  
   • Attend same-day in-person appointment for full neurological examination; cancel if symptoms resolve before the visit.  
   • Seek emergency care (A&E) sooner if new weakness, speech difficulty, gait disturbance, escalating pain, or uncontrollable vomiting occurs.
2. Health-related anxiety about serious intracranial pathology  
   • Provided reassurance that current presentation is most consistent with migraine; reinforced red-flag symptoms requiring urgent review.
3. Pregnancy risk addressed; patient reports pregnancy unlikely—no further action at this time.  
4. Verbal consent from patient has been obtained before using transcription software.

Subjective:
• Reason for visit: Sudden, severe left-sided headache with blurred vision and nausea.  
• History of presenting complaint  
  – Onset: ~4 hours ago; sudden.  
  – Location: Left side of head (described “kind of behind the eye”).  
  – Severity: 6/10 (kidney stone pain = 10/10 reference).  
  – Associated symptoms: Blurred vision with “zigzag lines,” dizziness, two episodes of vomiting, nausea, worse with movement, unable to tolerate screens.  
  – Tried paracetamol 3 hours ago—no relief.  
  – No limb weakness; gait normal.  
• Past medical history: Kidney stones (date unspecified).  
• Family history: Mother—migraines and hypothyroidism.  
• Medications: None regularly; paracetamol taken today (dose not documented).  
• Allergies: No known drug allergies.  
• Social history: Not discussed.  
• Pregnancy: Patient “really doubts” pregnancy.

Objective:
(No face-to-face exam performed in telehealth call)  
• Patient reports able to walk normally; no focal neurological deficits reported.  
• No vitals or physical findings documented.  
• No investigations performed.

Assessment & Plan:

1. Acute unilateral headache with visual disturbance  
   - Assessment: Migraine.  
   - Differential: Tension headache, cluster headache, intracranial pathology (e.g., stroke, tumor) – low likelihood given lack of focal deficits; patient safety-netted.  
   - Investigations: Plan for in-person neurological examination today.  
   - Treatment: Trial ibuprofen + antiemetic + sugary carbonated drink; escalate to specific migraine therapies if needed.  
   - Referral: None at this stage; consider urgent imaging if neurological signs emerge.

2. Health-related anxiety  
   - Assessment: Anxiety secondary to severe new headache.  
   - Treatment: Reassurance provided; advised on red-flag symptoms and when to seek urgent care.  
   - Referral: None; monitor at follow-up.
